_comment: Source of truth for the benchmark scenarios. Run bench/make_scenarios.py to rebuild bench/scenarios/. A turn's 'segments' are spoken pieces; 'pause_ms' after a segment is a real silence inside the same user turn (the turn must NOT end there).

scenarios.description: Short factual question. Pure latency test: the reply should be one short sentence.

segments.text: What's the capital of Australia?

scenarios.description: Casual small talk. The reply should sound like a person, not an assistant: short, warm, maybe one follow-up question.

segments.text: Hey, how's it going? I just got back from a really long walk and I'm kind of wiped out.

scenarios.description: Claude Code style question about the current repository. Needs tool use; the reply must still start fast (filler or early sentence) and be spoken, not markdown.

segments.text: So what does this repo actually do?

scenarios.description: Claude Code action request that takes time. Tests whether the system acknowledges at once and reports back conversationally.

segments.text: Can you run the tests and tell me if anything's broken?

scenarios.description: User hesitates with fillers and long pauses mid-sentence. The system must not cut in at either pause.

segments.text: I want to, um,
change the way the, uh,
the login page handles errors.

scenarios.description: Long rambling turn (about 25 s) with natural short pauses between clauses. Tests endpointing over a long turn, STT on long audio and a concise reply.

segments.text: Okay so here's the thing, I've been working on this side project for a couple of months now,
it's basically a little app that tracks what I eat and suggests recipes,
and it was going great at first, but lately every time I add a feature something else breaks,
and I'm starting to wonder if I should just rewrite the whole thing from scratch,
or if that's a terrible idea and I should just add tests and clean it up bit by bit.
What would you do?

scenarios.description: Three-turn follow-up chain. Turns 2 and 3 only make sense with context. Each next turn starts 600 ms after the assistant's previous reply audio ends.

segments.text: What's the difference between a process and a thread?
Okay, so which one is cheaper to create?
Huh. And why is that?

scenarios.description: User asks for something long, then interrupts 1500 ms after the assistant starts speaking. The assistant must stop fast and the next reply must follow the new request.

segments.text: Tell me about the history of the Roman Empire.
Actually, just give me the short version.

scenarios.description: Interruption deep into an explanation (4000 ms after assistant audio start) with a related question. The next reply should acknowledge what was already said and answer the new question.

segments.text: Can you explain how git rebase works?
Wait, wait, how is that different from merge?

scenarios.description: User corrects the assistant's reading of the request right after the first reply ends. The second reply must drop the first reading without long apologies.

segments.text: How do I undo my last commit?
No, I meant undo it but keep the changes.

scenarios.description: After the first reply, the user stays silent for 3.5 s, then says only 'yeah'. The system must not fill the silence with nagging, and must take the one-word turn as an answer.

segments.text: I'm thinking about renaming the main branch to trunk. Is that a bad idea?
Yeah.

scenarios.description: Syntactically incomplete pause with no filler ('I was wondering if' ... 1500 ms ... rest). Semantic endpointing must wait; plain silence VAD tends to cut in.

segments.text: I was wondering if
you could check what the readme says about installing.

scenarios.description: User says 'mm-hmm' 2500 ms into a long reply. This is a backchannel, not an interruption: the assistant should keep talking (or at most pause briefly and resume). Stopping and starting a new reply counts as a false barge-in.

segments.text: Walk me through how a hash map works.
Mm-hmm.
